title: Cataract Co-Management in Pine Beach, NJ | Academy Vision
metaDescription: Cloudy or dim vision? Academy Vision in Pine Beach monitors cataracts and coordinates with New Jersey eye surgeons for your care before and after surgery.
h1: Cataract Care Before and After Surgery in Pine Beach
lede:
Cataracts usually arrive slowly. Colors look a little faded, headlights start to glare, and reading needs more light than it used to. For many people, that gradual change eventually leads to a conversation about surgery.

At Academy Vision, we monitor cataracts as they progress and, when the time is right, coordinate with New Jersey eye surgeons so you receive expert care before and after surgery. From the first hazy signs to your recovery after the operation, your care stays connected.

sections.heading: How Cataracts Change Your Vision
sections.html:
A cataract is a clouding of the eye’s natural lens, the clear structure behind the iris that focuses light. Most cataracts are a normal part of aging and develop over years. Early on, an updated glasses prescription and brighter lighting can keep you comfortable.

Over time, the clouding can make night driving, reading, or seeing fine detail harder. When everyday tasks start to suffer, surgery to replace the cloudy lens with a clear artificial one is the usual next step, and that’s when a referral to an eye surgeon comes in.

sections.heading: Why It Helps to Start With Your Eye Doctor
sections.html:
• A clear diagnosis. A thorough exam shows whether a cataract is behind your symptoms or something else needs attention.
  • Options explained. Our optometrists take the time to explain what surgery involves and whether now is the right time.
  • A familiar team in the loop. Your Pine Beach eye doctor stays involved in your care before and after the operation.

sections.heading: Our Role Before and After Surgery
sections.html:
Co-management means your care is shared. An eye surgeon performs the operation, while your own eye doctor works alongside them. Before surgery, we follow your cataracts over time and help you weigh when surgery makes sense. Before and after the operation, we coordinate with your surgeon rather than simply handing you off.

Dr. Marc Ullman takes pride in offering honest second opinions and surgical consultations, which can help when you’re weighing a recommendation. Dr. Tyler Lesko is certified in Light Adjustable Lens technology, a type of lens implant whose prescription can be fine-tuned with light treatments after surgery.

sections.heading: Connected Care, Not a Hand-Off
sections.html:
Some referrals work like a hand-off: you’re sent to a surgeon, and your regular eye doctor hears little about what happens next. Coordinated care keeps the thread intact, so your history, any other eye conditions, and your everyday vision needs stay in view the whole way through.

After more than 40 years serving this area, we’ve seen how much it helps to have a familiar place to rely on when a big step like surgery comes along.

sections.heading: Related Care
sections.html: Cataracts are one of the conditions we manage as part of our medical eye care. For laser vision correction, our LASIK co-management follows the same shared approach with a local eye surgeon. And if it’s been a while since your last checkup, a comprehensive eye exam is the place to start.

faq.a: Cataract surgery is performed by an eye surgeon. Our part is to monitor your cataracts, help you understand your options, and coordinate with New Jersey eye surgeons for your care before and after the operation.

faq.q: When is the right time for cataract surgery?
faq.a: There’s usually no rush. Surgery is generally considered once a cataract starts getting in the way of things you need or love to do, like driving at night, reading, or a favorite hobby. Until then, regular checkups track how it’s changing. Other eye conditions or the demands of your work can shift the timing.

Cataract surgery is usually billed to medical insurance, while upgraded lens implants often add an out-of-pocket cost. The surgeon’s office can explain the costs of the operation itself, and our team will help check your benefits and explain what’s covered for your visits with us. You can see the plans we accept on our insurance page.

faq.q: What if something feels wrong after surgery?
faq.a: Follow your surgeon’s instructions and call their office promptly about increasing pain, redness, or blurring. Sudden vision loss, a curtain or shadow over your vision, or flashes of light with a sudden shower of new floaters need emergency care immediately.

cta.heading: Book a Cataract Evaluation in Pine Beach
cta.html: If glare, haze, or fading colors have been creeping into your days, let’s take a look. Call us at (732) 978-9306 or book your visit online, and we’ll help you understand what’s going on and what comes next.
